title: What mAh Really Means Explained Simply | PUC, CBSE and ISC
description:
Aarav reads the back of an old phone battery: 3.7 V and 5000 mAh. And when he plays a heavy game, the battery bar drops fast. What do these numbers really mean? In this animated lesson we open up cells and batteries.

First we see what is inside a cell (two electrodes and an electrolyte) and how a chemical reaction pushes electrons round a circuit. We compare primary cells (used once, like a 1.5 V dry cell) with secondary cells (rechargeable, like a 2 V lead acid cell and a 3.7 V lithium ion cell). On a live breadboard a real cell with internal resistance drives smaller and smaller loads while the readout and an oscilloscope show the terminal voltage falling as the current rises. We derive V = E - Ir step by step and plot it as a straight line, then explain capacity in milliampere hours (1 mAh = 3.6 C) and cells in series and in parallel. A worked example finds the charge, energy and battery life of a phone battery, followed by the exam trap (emf is not the terminal voltage), where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a fact card to screenshot.

This is Episode 59 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 9: Practical Electronic Components, their Specifications and PCB (Karnataka I PUC Electronics) | NCERT/CBSE Class 12 Physics Ch 3 Current Electricity: cells, emf, internal resistance, cells in series and parallel | ISC Class 12 Physics: Current Electricity (internal resistance, emf, combination of cells).
